post.description:
Verify a customer's Twilio credentials and list their numbers so the
connect modal becomes pick-from-list instead of type-the-number.

The credentials are used for ONE Twilio call and are NEVER logged or
persisted here — connect (POST /twilio/connect) is where the Auth Token
gets encrypted at rest.

put.description:
MERGE the provided top-level keys into twilio_automation_settings.

The FE sends partial objects (e.g. ``{"welcome": {...}}`` from the welcome
form, ``{"faq": {...}}`` from the FAQ form).  A full replace would wipe the
other sections, so we do a top-level dict merge: only the provided keys are
overwritten; absent keys are left untouched.

get.description:
Get Shopify customer context for a contact.

Returns customer data, orders, and abandoned carts if the contact
has received messages from a Shopify integration.

**Security**: User must own the instance to access contact data.

**Response Structure**:
- `hasShopify`: Boolean indicating if contact has Shopify interactions
- `found`: Boolean indicating if customer data was found in Shopify
- `customer`: Customer profile and statistics
- `orders`: List of recent orders (max 10)
- `abandonedCarts`: List of active abandoned carts (max 5)
- `shop`: Shop information

**Example Response**:
```json
{
  "hasShopify": true,
  "found": true,
  "customer": {
    "id": "gid://shopify/Customer/123",
    "firstName": "Alice",
    "lastName": "Johnson",
    "email": "alice@example.com",
    "stats": {
      "totalOrders": 5,
      "totalSpent": "450.00",
      "abandonedCartsCount": 1
    }
  },
  "orders": [...],
  "abandonedCarts": [...],
  "shop": {
    "id": 5,
    "domain": "mystore.myshopify.com"
  }
}
```

schema.title: Response Get Shopify Context Contacts  Phone  Shopify Context Get

get.description:
Lightweight check: does this contact have any Shopify interactions?

Returns a boolean flag. Uses two strategies:
1. Check Messages table for Shopify-platform messages (fast, no external API)
2. If no message found but instance has a connected shop, check Shopify GraphQL
   API for the customer (catches organic buyers)

Used by the frontend to decide whether to auto-open the Shopify context panel
and show the green dot indicator.

schema.title: Response Check Shopify Data Contacts  Phone  Shopify Check Get

Health check endpoint for Shopify database connection.

**Public endpoint** - no authentication required.

Returns the status of the Shopify database connection.
Useful for monitoring and debugging.

get.description:
Verify MegaSend token and return user's WhatsApp instances.

This endpoint:
1. Validates the X-MEGASEND-AUTH token
2. Retrieves user's WhatsApp instances
3. Returns response in format expected by Shopify app

Headers:
    X-MEGASEND-AUTH: The MegaSend API token

Query Params:
    shop: Shopify shop domain (optional)
Simple health check for Shopify integration.

Get list of Shopify stores connected to this user.

Implementation:
1. Retrieve all access tokens for the authenticated user
2. Decrypt each token to get the plaintext mega_token
3. Query Shopify database to find shops using each mega_token
4. Return aggregated list of shops found

This ensures the user only sees shops they have access to via their tokens.

post.description:
Select a Shopify store for AI integration.

This endpoint accepts shop_id and shop_domain from the frontend
and stores them directly in ai_settings without validation.
The frontend (Shopify app) is responsible for ensuring the user
owns the selected shop.

**Agent Support**:
Agents can select Shopify stores if they have `can_send_messages` permission on the instance.

get.description: List Shopify products available for sync to WhatsApp catalog.

post.description: Sync selected Shopify products to WhatsApp catalog.

get.summary: Get Shopify conversion analytics for a campaign
get.description:
Returns Shopify conversion metrics for a campaign including:
    - Overview: conversions, revenue, conversion rate, avg order value
    - Funnel: sent → delivered → read → purchased
    - ROI: message cost vs revenue earned
    - Top converters: recipients who made purchases

    If no Shopify shop is connected, returns has_shopify=false.
    Analytics are computed automatically when a campaign completes,
    and refreshed periodically for 7 days to catch late orders.

post.summary: Refresh Shopify analytics for a campaign
post.description: Triggers a background re-computation of Shopify conversion analytics. Results are delivered via WebSocket.

get.description: Paginated list of recipients with Shopify conversion enrichment. Filter by customer status.

BusinessHoursConfig.title: BusinessHoursConfig
BusinessHoursConfig.description:
Weekly business-hours schedule for the away_message automation.

Client submits this as the ``business_hours_config`` field when saving an
away message. Timezone is an IANA name (e.g. ``Asia/Jerusalem``, ``UTC``).

enabled.title: Enabled
enabled.description: Whether this day has an active window

start.title: Start
start.description: Window start time in HH:MM 24h local time

end.title: End
end.description: Window end time in HH:MM 24h local time

BusinessHoursDay.title: BusinessHoursDay
BusinessHoursDay.description:
One day of the weekly business-hours schedule.

- ``enabled=false``  → the entire day is outside business hours
- ``start >= end``   → the window wraps past midnight (e.g. 22:00 → 02:00)

TwilioAutomationSettings.title: TwilioAutomationSettings
TwilioAutomationSettings.description:
MERGE-friendly body for PUT /twilio/{id}/automation-settings.

All top-level keys optional so the FE can POST only the section it owns.
model_dump(exclude_unset=True) drives the top-level merge in the route.

TwilioPhoneNumbersRequest.title: TwilioPhoneNumbersRequest
TwilioPhoneNumbersRequest.description:
POST /twilio/phone-numbers — verify creds and list SMS-capable numbers so
the connect modal is pick-from-list. Creds used for ONE call, never logged
or persisted.

TelnyxAutomationSettings.title: TelnyxAutomationSettings
TelnyxAutomationSettings.description:
Flexible MERGE-friendly body for PUT /telnyx/{id}/automation-settings.

All top-level keys are optional so the FE can POST only the section it
owns (welcome form, faq form, etc.) without wiping the others.
`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` is used for the top-level merge.

TelnyxPhoneNumbersRequest.title: TelnyxPhoneNumbersRequest
TelnyxPhoneNumbersRequest.description:
POST /telnyx/phone-numbers — verify a customer's Telnyx API key and list
their SMS-capable numbers so the connect modal is pick-from-list. The key
is used for ONE outbound Telnyx call and is never logged or persisted.

Mobile019AutomationSettings.title: Mobile019AutomationSettings
Mobile019AutomationSettings.description:
MERGE-friendly body for PUT /019mobile/{id}/automation-settings — all
top-level keys optional (FE posts one section at a time). Validated with the
same _validate_faq logic as TelnyxAutomationSettings.

InforUAutomationSettings.title: InforUAutomationSettings
InforUAutomationSettings.description:
MERGE-friendly body for PUT /inforumobile/{id}/automation-settings.
All top-level keys optional so the FE posts only the section it owns.
model_dump(exclude_unset=True) drives the top-level merge (LLD 04).

InforUConnectRequest.title: InforUConnectRequest
InforUConnectRequest.description:
POST /inforumobile/connect. BYO InforU account: username + token are the
credential pair; sender is the registered alphanumeric Sender ID. All stay
schema-Optional so the SERVICE enforces requiredness (400
'inforu_credentials_required' naming the missing fields) and can exempt
INFORUMOBILE_DRY_RUN for tests/local — mirrors the Telnyx connect contract.

InforUVerifyRequest.title: InforUVerifyRequest

LineAutomationSettings.title: LineAutomationSettings
LineAutomationSettings.description:
Partial, MERGE-friendly body for PUT /line/{id}/automation-settings.

All top-level keys optional so the FE can POST only the section it owns
(welcome form, faq form, ...) without wiping the others. The route uses
model_dump(exclude_unset=True) for a top-level dict merge, exactly like
the Telegram automation-settings endpoint.

CalendarEventEntry.title: CalendarEventEntry
CalendarEventEntry.description:
One event already on the user's Google calendar.

Deliberately narrow: enough to draw a block on the grid and open the real
thing in Google, and nothing more. Attendees, conferencing details,
attachments and the description are all left upstream.
